comments.comment: The video was generally very accurate, but as a native Dane I managed to spot 3 minor mistakes:  1 (4:47): It is very true that Danes, Swedes and Norwegians can generally understand each other speaking their own languages, but this does not include Iceland. I do not understand a word of Icelandic, and this is true for the vast majority of Danes. The biggest reason that Danes are still able to communicate easily with Icelanders is because they learn Danish in school. (Also, it was kinda weird of you to include a clip of Finnish speaking guy. I literally didn't understand a word of what he said)  2 (7:59): This is somewhat innacurate as Denmark only joined the European Communities in 1973 and was not a founding member of the European Coal and Steel Community, although it is true that Denmark participated in the transformation of the EU from the EC to the EU in 1993.  3 (1:10): This isn't so much a correction rather than a comment. The Danish regional system is extremely insignificant in Danish society and is in no way similar to the regional systems of a country like France for example, where Regional divisions play a much more significant cultural and political role in society. If you ask most Danes, I doubt that they would even know the names of all of the 5 regions. The reason Denmark has these 'regions' is because the Regional Councils subside over the budgets of hospitals, psychiatric institutions and similar medical facilities in their respective regions. You would NEVER hear a Dane say, "Oh, I am from the Region of Midtjylland- how about you?".  Overall, though, good content. Keep it up.
